questions.question: Name five things that soil contains, and describe how to show that soil contains air.
questions.expected_answer: Soil contains rock grains, air, water, dead remains that rot into humus, and living things such as earthworms, ants, fungi and bacteria. To show it contains air, drop a dry lump of soil into a glass of water: bubbles of air rise out of the spaces between the grains.

questions.question: Compare sandy, clayey and loamy soil.
questions.expected_answer: Sandy soil has big grains, feels gritty, does not hold together, and lets water drain through quickly, so it dries out fast and holds few minerals. Clayey soil has tiny grains, feels smooth and sticky when wet, holds a lot of water, can get waterlogged and cracks and goes hard when dry. Loamy soil is a mixture of sand, silt and clay with humus; it is dark and crumbly, holds enough water but drains well, and is best for most plants.

questions.question: Describe the drainage test and its results.
questions.expected_answer: Three funnels lined with cotton wool are filled with the same amount of sandy, clayey and loamy soil, and the same amount of water is poured onto each; only the type of soil is changed. After the same time, the water that drained through is measured. Most water drains through sandy soil, least through clayey soil, and loamy soil is in between.
